[[File:Peter P. Marra1030626.jpg|thumb|Image of Peter P. Marra]]
'''Peter P. Marra''' is an American [[ornithologist]], [[Conservationist (biology)|conservationist]], and educator. Marra is the Founding Director and Dean of the Earth Commons and a biology professor at [[Georgetown University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Georgetown University Faculty Directory |url=https://gufaculty360.georgetown.edu/s/contact/0031Q000020XbIrQAK/peter-marra |access-date=2025-04-25 |website=gufaculty360.georgetown.edu |language=en-US}}</ref> Marra is a former director of the [[Smithsonian Migratory Bird Center]]. Marra is best known for his research on domesticated and feral cats and their impact on bird populations.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |date=2018-10-01 |title=2018 Elliott Coues Award to Peter P. Marra |url=https://academic.oup.com/auk/article/135/4/1189/5149020 |journal=The Auk |volume=135 |issue=4 |pages=1189 |doi=10.1642/AUK-18-119.1 |issn=1938-4254}}</ref>

== Career ==
Marra earned a B.S. in biology and chemistry from [[Southern Connecticut State University]], an M.S. in zoology from [[Louisiana State University]] in 1989, and a Ph.D. in ecology from [[Dartmouth College]] in 1998.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Pete Marra |url=https://global.si.edu/people/pete-marra |access-date=2025-04-25 |website=global.si.edu}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Pongsajapan |first=Robert |date=2019-04-03 |title=Leading Smithsonian Scientist to Direct Georgetown Environment Initiative |url=https://www.georgetown.edu/news/leading-smithsonian-scientist-to-direct-georgetown-environment-initiative/ |access-date=2025-04-25 |website=Georgetown University |language=en-US}}</ref> From 1999 to 2019, Marra worked as a researcher and the director of the [[Smithsonian Migratory Bird Center]].<ref name=":0" /> In 2019, Marra was appointed Dean of the Earth Commons, Institute for Environment & Sustainability, and Laudato Si’ Professor of Biology and the Environment at [[Georgetown University]].<ref name=":0" />

Marra has founded bird conservancy projects including Neighborhood Nestwatch, The Migratory Connectivity Project, and the Animal Mortality and Monitoring Program.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Peter Marra |url=https://www.manomet.org/our_people/peter-marra/ |access-date=2025-04-26 |website=Manomet Conservation Sciences |language=en-US}}</ref>

Marra was awarded the 2018 [[Elliott Coues]] Award for his contribution to ornithology.<ref name=":2" />

== Publications ==
Among some 260+ publications authored, coauthored, or edited by Marra:

* Linking Winter and Summer Events in a Migratory Bird by Using Stable-Carbon Isotopes (1998) [[Digital object identifier|DOI]]:[[doi:10.1126/science.282.5395.1884|10.1126/science.282.5395.1884]]
* Links between worlds: unraveling migratory connectivity (2002) [[Digital object identifier|DOI]]:[[doi:10.1016/S0169-5347(01)02380-1|10.1016/S0169-5347(01)02380-1]]
* The impact of free-ranging domestic cats on wildlife of the United States (2013)  [[Digital object identifier|DOI]]:[[doi:10.1038/ncomms2380|10.1038/ncomms2380]]
* Cat Wars: The Devastating Consequences of a Cuddly Killer (2016) {{ISBN|9780691167411}}
* Decline of the North American avifauna (2019) [[Digital object identifier|DOI]]:[[doi:10.1126/science.aaw1313|10.1126/science.aaw1313]]
